title: Circuit Breaker

validation.research: Six primary references: Michael Nygard’s Release It! publisher catalog; Martin Fowler’s Circuit Breaker explanation and Nygard attribution; Microsoft’s state/classification/resource-scope guidance; Resilience4j documentation for configurable windows/minimum samples/slow calls/probes and concurrency separation; Polly documentation for retained scope, lazy half-open transitions and no implicit retries; Marc Brooker’s AWS discussion of retry pressure, uncertain outcomes and modal recovery tradeoffs. Singular Circuit Breaker is the established title and the old plural title remains an alias. Original warehouse, rate-window/minimum-sample, independent supplier/shard, uncertain-write and provenance-labelled catalog fallback contexts are retained. The small virtual-time code, chosen thresholds, trace and native diagrams are original teaching material.

runnable_example.verification: Actual article fences run unchanged on Python 3.11+. Exact seven-line output and six-request/four-invocation trace match every figure row. Two counted failures open; successful/falsy results reset history; ignored ValueError, unclassified TimeoutError and cancellation-like BaseException preserve closed-state counter and error identity. Cooldown starts at failure completion with arbitrary clock origin, rejects just before expiry, admits at equality/afterward, and local rejection changes neither deadline nor counts nor invokes the callback. Time advancement alone performs no background transition. Failed probes restart cooldown at their completion; successful probes close/reset, and a later isolated failure does not immediately reopen. Inconclusive/error/cancelled probes propagate unchanged, reopen without incrementing failure count and release actual callback-owned TemporaryFiles. A sequential reentry seam exercises busy-probe rejection without claiming thread safety. Independent breakers isolate scopes; newly created instances do not share history. Real files close before caller observation and callbacks own that cleanup. No network, concurrency synchronization, fleet sharing, timer thread, deadline enforcement, retry, durable batch/fallback implementation or remote rollback is inferred.

example_limits: Existing canonical data-circuit-breakers is revised in place, preserving ID, URL, Data Engineering tags/verse, warehouse resource-exhaustion scenario, versioned catalog fallback, supplier/shard scoping, window/sample teaching context and primary state-figure asset path. Established singular Circuit Breaker becomes the title; former title Circuit Breakers remains an alias. Its one primary home moves to Reliability and Failure Handling; former Execution & recovery retains a cross-link and thirteen other members. Historical Data Engineering import metadata is unchanged and original article/SVG are archived locally. Original Python 3.11+ single-caller virtual-time simulation retains one breaker. Two counted DependencyFailure outcomes since the last success open it; 100 ms cooldown starts at failure completion. A subsequent call at or after the boundary is one half-open probe. Probe success resets history; failed/inconclusive probes reopen; nondependency errors/cancellation propagate and do not increment the counted-failure total. Action-owned cleanup precedes returning/raising. Six sequential requests cause four callback invocations and two local rejections. No network, timer thread, rate window, slow-call detection, concurrent synchronization, fleet sharing, timeout, automatic retry, batch persistence, fallback implementation or remote rollback is supplied. Tests verify exact threshold, falsy-success reset, classification/error identity, local rejection without execution or state/deadline extension, arbitrary clock origin and cooldown from failure completion, lazy transitions and exact before/at/after boundaries, probe failure/restart, reset after recovery, inconclusive cancellation/error probes, real callback-owned TemporaryFile closure and scope isolation. A sequential reentry seam exercises the explicit busy-probe guard only and supplies no concurrency guarantee. No claim is made that the breaker closes unknown resources; callback cleanup is a stated precondition. In-memory diagnostic fields and a virtual clock expose the teaching state, with no real service or timer.
